title: A versatile nuclei extraction protocol for single cell multiome ATAC and gene expression
author: Rose Ruiz Daniels
materials: The nuclei are also counted using a Bio-Rad TC20 to confirm results from the disposable haemocytometer and to count the proportion of viable cells. Nuclei are identified as “dead”, therefore a good nuclei isolation will have a small percentage of live cells. 1-4% of live cells is ideal. High proportions of live cells indicates incomplete nuclear isolation and could be an indication of high amounts of debris or insufficient lysis time.

steps.title: Keep samples frozen and pre‑chill equipment
steps.instruction: Keep samples on dry ice until immediately before nuclei isolation; perform all handling on ice; pre‑chill the centrifuge to 4 °C; place a piece of frozen tissue into one well of a 6‑well tissue‑culture plate containing 1 mL TST; if the tissue sticks to the cryotube, remove it with tweezers while still on dry ice and transfer to the plate; avoid processing after flash‑freezing.

steps.title: Mince tissue on ice
steps.instruction: On ice, mince the tissue with Tungsten Carbide scissors for 30 seconds, then continue with Noyes Spring Scissors (Fine Science Tools Catalog #15514‑12) for a total of 10 minutes. Use this sequence for hard tissues (fin, skin); for softer tissues use spring scissors for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Gentle pipetting in dissociation buffer
steps.instruction: After 5 minutes of mincing, gently pipette the suspension up and down with a P1000 pipette using a low‑retention filtered tip for 5 minutes while keeping the sample on ice. Assess timing by nuclear appearance (refer to provided images). If staining nuclei with trypan blue, do so promptly because nuclei degrade quickly when not kept on ice.

steps.title: Filter lysate
steps.instruction: Pass the lysate through a 40 µm cell strainer and immediately add an additional 1 mL TST to the strainer.

steps.title: Add ST buffer to lysate
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL freshly prepared ST buffer to the filtered lysate.

steps.title: Transfer lysate to tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the 5 mL lysate into a marked 15 mL Falcon tube (Corning) kept on ice.

steps.title: Centrifuge nuclei
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 500 × g, 4 °C for 5 minutes in a swinging‑bucket rotor.

steps.title: Remove supernatant and resuspend nuclei
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant; use a P200 pipette to carefully remove excess liquid without disturbing the pellet. Resuspend the pellet gently with a P1000 pipette in diluted nuclei buffer aiming for a target recovery of ~6,000 nuclei. Include RNase inhibitor at 1 U/µL. Adjust the resuspension volume to pellet size (typically 100 µL–1,000 µL; use 400 µL for skin/fin; up to 1 mL if many nuclei).

steps.title: Count nuclei
steps.instruction: Count nuclei using a C‑chip disposable haemocytometer (or a non‑disposable haemocytometer). Observe nuclear integrity and debris level while counting.
